security_spec.violation_condition: When XiangShan implements Zimop (treating TEB/MDB/DPB as functional NOPs via the Zimop encoding) but does NOT implement Zisb barrier semantics in the pipeline control logic. Specifically: (1) Decoder maps TEB/MDB/DPB to no-op micro-ops without asserting a speculation barrier control signal; (2) Branch predictor continues to speculatively fetch/execute instructions after TEB before the preceding branch resolves; (3) Load-Store unit permits a load after MDB to bypass an older unresolved store's address check; (4) Execution units permit instructions after DPB to consume data-value predictions from instructions before DPB. In each case, the hardware functionally executes correctly (instructions retire as NOPs) but fails to enforce the microarchitectural speculation boundaries mandated by the spec.
security_spec.summary: Zisb speculation barrier instructions (TEB/MDB/DPB) encoded via Zimop may be silently treated as no-ops without enforcing microarchitectural speculation boundaries, allowing Spectre-class transient execution attacks to bypass software-inserted barriers and leak secrets through cache-based side channels
